pointers.sentence: A project that defines them and no `MAILERS` still sends mail through them (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:get_connection`; [What changed in mail and tasks](mail-and-tasks.md)).

One that the settings module defines warns as the module loads (`django/conf/__init__.py:Settings.__init__`); one set by `LazySettings.configure`, `override_settings` or an assignment warns as it is set; the first read warns, and the settings object then keeps the value, so that later reads do not warn while it is kept.
A value that Django's own code read first therefore warns no later reader (`django/conf/__init__.py:_show_settings_deprecation_warning`).

A settings module, or one call of `LazySettings.configure`, that defines both is refused with `ImproperlyConfigured` (`django/conf/__init__.py:_check_email_settings_conflicts`), where 5.2.17 and 6.0.8 load it.
Where `MAILERS` is defined, an email setting cannot be read, even one left at its default (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.__getattr__`).

Since 5.2 `BaseCommand.execute` takes its arguments for `BaseCommand.check` from `BaseCommand.get_check_kwargs`, which a command may override (`django/core/management/base.py:BaseCommand.get_check_kwargs`): migrate adds its database, and runserver names an empty set of tags, which selects no check, and runs the checks itself, naming no tags, as it starts serving (`django/core/management/commands/runserver.py:Command.inner_run`).

`CheckRegistry.run_checks` used to pass on `None`, which Django's checks read as no database; at this commit it passes every configured alias, and, where no tags are named either, leaves out the checks tagged database (`django/core/checks/registry.py:CheckRegistry.run_checks`).

The aliases reach the model checks, which are not tagged database: a field's backend checks ask MySQL's backend for the field's column type (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field._check_backend_specific_checks`), and the backend connects to learn its features (`django/db/backends/mysql/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.mysql_server_data`).

The aliases reach the model checks, which are not tagged database: a field's backend checks ask MySQL's backend for the field's column type (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field._check_backend_specific_checks`), and the backend connects to learn its features (`django/db/backends/mysql/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.mysql_server_data`).
The notes say that callers "should be prepared for databases to be accessed" (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`; [The system checks](../commands/checks.md)).

`ManagementUtility.execute` reads `settings.INSTALLED_APPS` before it looks a command up, and catches and keeps the `ImproperlyConfigured` that loading the settings may raise (`django/core/management/__init__.py:ManagementUtility.execute`).
At this commit `Settings.__init__` turns into `ImproperlyConfigured` an `ImportError` that names the settings module itself (`django/conf/__init__.py:Settings.__init__`).

`ManagementUtility.fetch_command` then refuses, with the exception's message and status 1, a command whose `BaseCommand.requires_settings` is true, the default; startproject, startapp, shell and makemessages set it false (`django/core/management/__init__.py:ManagementUtility.fetch_command`).

The 6.2 notes say `BaseCommand.requires_settings` makes configurable "whether to suppress an ImportError escaping from a settings module" (`docs/releases/6.2.txt`); at this commit it decides only where loading the settings raises `ImproperlyConfigured`.

In 6.0 the settings module that startproject writes (`django/conf/project_template/project_name/settings.py-tpl`) lost `DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD`, and startapp's class lost `AppConfig.default_auto_field`, both `BigAutoField` under 5.2.17, whose default was `AutoField`; 6.0 made `BigAutoField` the default and removed the lines (`docs/releases/6.0.txt`).

Since 6.0 both commands make a missing target directory, parents and all, where 5.2.17 refused (`django/core/management/templates.py:TemplateCommand.handle`).

Since 5.2 the shell fills its namespace before it starts, from the dotted paths `Command.get_auto_imports` returns (`django/core/management/commands/shell.py:Command.get_auto_imports`): in 5.2 the models that `Apps.get_models` lists, and from 6.0, before them, the settings object, the default connection, `django.db.models`, `django.db.models.functions`, `reset_queries` and `django.utils.timezone` ([The commands Django ships](../commands/builtin.md#the-shell)).
